entries.title: The $750 billion converged living room: a plateau approaches
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that global sales of smartphones, tablets, PCs, TV sets and video game consoles will exceed $750 billion in 2014, up $50 billion from 2013
entries.metric: global sales of smartphones, tablets, PCs, TVs and consoles
entries.subject: Consumer device revenue

entries.title: Wearables: the eyes have it
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that smart glasses, fitness bands and watches, should sell about 10 million units in 2014, generating $3 billion.
entries.metric: unit sales of smart glasses, fitness bands and watches
entries.subject: Wearables

entries.title: One became many: the tablet market stratifies
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in the first quarter of 2014, the installed base of compact tablets (with screens smaller than 8.5 inches) will surpass the base of classic tablets (8.5 inches and larger) for the first time.
entries.metric: compact tablet installed base end Q1 2014
entries.subject: Tablets

entries.title: Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs): not disruptive yet, but the future looks bright
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that by 2014, student registrations in Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) will be up 100 percent compared to 2012 to over 10 million courses, but ... less than 0.2 percent of all tertiary education-equivalent courses completed in 2014 will be MOOCs.
entries.subject: MOOCs

entries.title: eVisits: the 21st century housecall
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2014, there will be 100 million eVisits globally, potentially saving over $5 billion when compared to the cost of in-person doctor visits
entries.subject: Telehealth (eVisits)

entries.title: Doubling up on pay-TV
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that by the end of 2014 up to 50 million homes around the world will have two or more separate pay-television subscriptions, with the additional subscriptions generating about $5 billion in revenues.
entries.metric: homes with two or more pay-TV subscriptions
entries.subject: Pay TV and SVOD subscriptions

entries.title: Television measurement: for better and worse
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2014 the measurement of domestic television program viewing should become more accurate in a number of countries, including Germany and the UK, because of the introduction of hybrid measurement.
entries.subject: TV audience measurement

entries.title: Broadcast sports rights: premium plus
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2014 the value of premium sports broadcast rights worldwide will increase to $24.2 billion, a 14 percent rise, or $2.9 billion over 2013.
entries.metric: worldwide premium sports broadcast rights value
entries.subject: Sports broadcast rights

entries.title: Performance rights lift recorded music revenues
entries.quote: In 2014 Deloitte predicts that revenues from performance rights, a license payable for the right to play music to the public, should exceed one billion dollars for the first time.
entries.subject: Music performance rights

entries.title: 'Cordless' video-on-demand leaps in Sub-Saharan Africa
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2014 the number of video-on-demand (VOD) users in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) will grow by about one million – despite the lack of broadband infrastructure in the region.
entries.metric: growth in VOD users in Sub-Saharan Africa
entries.subject: Video on demand in Africa

entries.title: Short messaging services versus instant messaging: value versus volume
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2014 instant messaging services on mobile phones (MIM) will carry more than twice the volume (50 billion versus 21 billion per day) of messages sent via a short messaging service (SMS).
entries.subject: Mobile instant messaging vs SMS

entries.title: Phablets are not a phad
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2014 shipments of phablets, smartphones with 5.0-6.9 inch screens will represent a quarter of smartphones sold, or 300 million units.
entries.subject: Phablets

entries.title: The smartphone generation gap: over-55? There's no app for that
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2014, the over-55s will be the age group experiencing the fastest year-on-year rises in smartphone penetration across developed markets.
entries.subject: Smartphone adoption among over-55s

entries.title: 'Ruggedized' data devices at $250: reinventing the business case for mobile field force
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2014 the entry price for a ruggedized, connected data device ... will fall to $250.
entries.metric: entry price of rugged connected data device
entries.subject: Rugged mobile devices

notes: Launched 14 January 2014 (Deloitte collection page). PDF read from the Internet Archive copy; the deloitte.com file now returns an error. Deloitte published a report card for this edition: '13 of the 14 predictions hitting a more than 70% accuracy rate' (Deloitte's self-assessment, see INDEX.md).
